div.head: Wif 1
div.ab: Gif man mædan oððe wif weddian wille, 7 hit swa hire 7 freondan gelicege, ðonne is riht, þæt se brydguma æfter Godes rihte 7 æfter woroldgerysnum ærest behate 7 on wedde sylle ðam m̃, ðe hire forspecan syn, þæt he on ða wisan hire geornige, ðe he hy æfter Godes rihte healdan wille, swa wær his wif sceal; 7 aborgian his frind þæt.

Si quis uirginem uel uiduam ducere uelit, et hoc illi placeat et amicis suis, tunc rectum est, ut brudgume per Dei iusticiam et seculi competens inprimis promittat et uadiet eis, qui paranimphi sunt, quod eo modo querat eam, ut secundum Dei rectum pertenere uelit, sicut sponsus debet legitimam sponsam; et plegient hoc amici sui.

Gif man mædan oððe wif weddian wille, 7 hit swa hire 7 freondan gelicige, ðonne is riht, ðæt se brydguma æfter Godes rihte 7 æfter woroldgerysnum ærest behate 7 on wedde sylle ðam, ðe hire forsprecan synd, þæt he on ða wisan hire geornige, ðet he hy æfter Godes rihte healdan wille, swa wær his wif sceal; 7 aborgian his frind ðæt.

Wenn man ein Mädchen oder eine Frau verloben will, indem dies ihr und den [Bluts]freunden [beider Brautleute] so genehm ist, dann ist richtig, dass der Bräutigam gemäss religiöser Pflicht und gemäss bürgerlichen Rechtsgewohnheiten denen, die ihre [der Braut] Vorsprecher sind, zuerst verheisse und kraft Pfandes förmlich gelobe, dass er ihrer in dér Weise begehre, auf dass er sie nach Gottes [vollkommenem] Recht halten wolle, wie ein Mann sein Eheweib [behandeln] soll; und dies sollen seine [Bluts]freunde verbürgen.

If anyone wishes to betroth a maiden or a woman, and it is agreeable to her and to the [blood-]friends [of both parties], then it is right that the bridegroom, according to God's law and according to secular custom, should first promise and formally pledge to those who are her [the bride's] advocates that he seeks her in such a way that he will keep her according to God's [perfect] law, as a man should [treat] his wife; and let his [blood-]friends stand surety for this.

If a man wishes to betroth a maiden or a widow, and it so pleases her and her kinsmen, then it is right that the bridegroom first according to God's law and proper secular custom should promise and pledge to those who are her advocates, that he desires her in such a way that he will maintain her according to God's law as a man should maintain his wife; and his friends are to stand surety for it.
div.note: B's ‘m̃’ means ‘men’; Liebermann would strike it or correct to ‘mannum’. B's ‘gelicege’ was altered late to ‘-cige’. In the Quadripartitus the meaning ‘marry’ remains later with ‘weddian’ alone. Liebermann compares II Cn 74 and Swer 1.
